ordering: parsers, mounts, and routes are each in source order within their file; cross-file order is path order, not execution order (see limitations)
limitations: Regex-based static scan: misses dynamic route registration, computed path strings, and middleware passed as a spread array.

Route-shaped text inside string literals (docs, fixtures, multi-line templates) will appear in the map; comments are stripped, strings are not. A visible false positive beats a silently dropped route.
Middleware chains are read from the route declaration onward; a chain assembled across multiple statements before the route is registered will be incomplete.
A regex literal containing a quote character can desync argument splitting for that one call, truncating its reported chain.
Mount-to-file resolution follows simple const-require patterns only.

Ordering within a file is reliable. Ordering ACROSS files is alphabetical by path, not execution order, so a parser mounted in one file and a router in another cannot be sequenced from this output alone.
Treat this map as a starting inventory to verify with Read and Grep, not as proof of absence.
